Maya Tran: Quick sanity check  weekly KPI shows a small lift on launch day but then noise after day 4. wondering if this is real or measurement artifacts :thinking_face:
Evan Cole: which metric? conversion to trial or MQL?
Maya Tran: DAU->trial. lift ~+12% on day 1, then drifts to baseline by day 5. suspicious pattern for paid social bursts
Zara Liu: could be attribution window mismatch or partner deduping. we swapped partner keys for SocialBeta last week, right?
Jorge Rivas: yes we normalized SocialBeta tags in the backfill run attr-20260330. that could reassign some earlier clicks to different dates/channels
Tom B: pulseboard reads raw event uids; exec deck pulls CRM MQLs post-backfill. different pipelines = different stories. small UI fix: add an "ingestion vs event" toggle on the KPI chart
Maya Tran: good call. before we change anything, can we run a quick parity check: raw events vs crm-backfilled series for the launch cohort? simple SQL is fine
Jorge Rivas: running now. snippet i'm using: ```
SELECT cohort_day, source_type, count(distinct user_id) as trials
FROM (
  SELECT user_id, date_trunc('day', event_time) AS cohort_day, 'raw' AS source_type
  FROM events WHERE campaign='spring_launch' AND event='trial_start'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT user_id, date_trunc('day', crm_ingest_time) AS cohort_day, 'crm' AS source_type
  FROM crm_events WHERE campaign='spring_launch' AND event='trial_start'
) t
GROUP BY cohort_day, source_type
ORDER BY cohort_day, source_type;```
Evan Cole: thanks. also include a filter for utm_campaign IS NULL to isolate organic direct traffic (helps see if paid reassignments caused the spike)
Zara Liu: FYI webinar redirect team reported a short-lived proxy that stripped utms for ~90 registrations on launch day. that would inflate "direct" and deflate partner numbers
Maya Tran: that matches the timing. if those 90 are high-intent, they could move the conversion shape a bit on day 1
ops-bot: Job complete: parity-diff attr-20260330 finished at 2026-03-30T11:12:03Z. rows_processed=8,412.
Jorge Rivas: uploaded CSV with both series and a delta column: https://redwood.internal/files/spring_launch_parity_307654.csv :file_folder:
Evan Cole: quick read: raw shows a +12% day1 spike, crm-backed series shows +5%. delta concentrated in direct and SocialBeta. looks like partial reclassification after backfill
Maya Tran: so some of the lift is real but magnitude changes with attribution. need to decide canonical metric for the weekly deck and add a short note explaining the variance
Tom B: I'd vote: weekly deck = crm-backed MQLs (single source of truth for revenue ops), but pulseboard default = raw events. add a badge on slides: "canonical: crm-backed (run attr-20260330)"
Zara Liu: agree. also add a small control: include a "raw vs crm" sparkline on the KPI slide for transparency so PMs can see delta at a glance
Evan Cole: will draft the 2-line note for PMs: summary + link to CSV + % estimate moved. putting it in the weekly deck appendix
Maya Tran: action items: Jorge add CSV link to deck, Evan write the note, Tom implement badge + sparkline toggle, Zara add a pre-launch redirect checklist for webinars
Jorge Rivas: CSV link posted in assets. also included CI bounds in the sheet
ops-bot: Calendar: "KPI parity review" scheduled 2026-03-30T11:45:00Z, duration 20m. invited: Maya Tran, Evan Cole, Jorge Rivas, Zara Liu, Tom B
Maya Tran: appreciate the quick triage team. long-term: add an "attribution parity" automated test in the weekly KPI pipeline so this flags earlier before deck freeze
Evan Cole: +1. i'll sketch the test (compare raw vs crm delta > 8% -> flag) and put in the data runbook
Tom B: will prototype the KPI badge and sparkline today in staging
Zara Liu: adding redirect checklist to the webinar playbook now. will ping ops when it's ready
Maya Tran: OK closing thread. we'll review in the parity review meeting and finalize the exec note. thanks :thumbsup:
